arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Katyal argued that Laroe would lack standing if it filed its own lawsuit.
Mr. Dvoretzky argued that Article III does not dictate who can join an existing case.
Justice Kagan asked about the difference between claims in relief and other claims.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests whether federal courts must verify Article III standing for mandatory intervenors. The Town of Chester seeks to dismiss Laroe Estates for lack of standing. Laroe Estates wants to join the existing lawsuit as a full party.

paragraphs: The Town of Chester argues Article III requires a case or controversy for all parties.
Laroe Estates argues Rule 24(a)(2) creates full party status independent of standing.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This dispute defines the procedural entry point for third parties in federal litigation. It determines whether courts must screen every new party for constitutional injury. The outcome shapes the scope of federal judicial power and case management efficiency.
